Asarta (L96)

Region (English scoring-table division): Sarhal.

In one sentence: Play the Riverclaw brother whom the naga did not choose, then use sea trade, mutation and personal achievement to prove to all lizardfolk that prophecy can be rewritten.

Story: high | Mission-tree length: medium (20 L96-exclusive missions; the formed country is separate) | Mission-tree status: use the current local scripts supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: high | Tedium: medium (sibling rivalry and event prerequisites) | Early pressure: medium-high | Expansion: medium-high

The brother who was not chosen

In 1444, Asarta is already an independent Arraskay lizardfolk tribal country. L96's history file gives it its own provinces, the Riverclaw Katyradz, naga religious privileges and a historical friendship with Rayaz. Rayaz's ruler Sykar is his brother, yet the naga chose him as the forerunner of the “Final Empire”. Current narrative text makes Asarta's motive intensely personal: Katyradz refuses to remain a supporting character to his elder brother and intends to prove himself through the capture of great cities, cultural revival and the Final Empire. The sibling relationship belongs to the opening background; defeating the rival and rewriting the prophecy are the player's future route.【Local history script】【Local flavour text】

The offline English Wiki has no dedicated Asarta country-history page. Its Countries during the Greentide list only places Asarta among the Riverclaw tribes alongside Rayaz; the Anzara Empire page supplies broader regional background and contains two conflicting end dates, 1453 and 1454. These sources are not enough to establish a detailed foundation chronology for Asarta, and they cannot replace the Mod's account of Katyradz's motives.【Wiki source】

More than a recoloured Rayaz

Both brothers can eventually pursue Khatalashya, but L96 has its own mission tree before formation and is not L95 under another name. The opening focuses on rival cities, restoring Irikin culture and extending riverboat trade; coastal development requires an actual fleet, ports and a network of goods. Missions and flavour text introduce merfolk escorts, seafaring lizardfolk and ambitions reaching into the gulf, giving Asarta a distinctly different map rhythm from Rayaz's river integration.【Local script】【Local flavour text】

The middle section's “Herald of Change” pushes the political rivalry into the supernatural. Naga mutation privileges, related events and mission prerequisites repeatedly make the player answer demands and seek powers beyond the prophecy. Katyradz must show the naga that their choice was wrong while also watching for the true Herald of Change. The ending does not simply declare victory; it even imagines a failure in which future generations must understand why the country fell. This is mission-set fiction and an optional campaign outcome, not history already completed in 1444.【Local script】【Local flavour text】

The maritime chapter is not unconditional expansion. After an early riverboat disaster, merfolk rescue the sailors and later ask Asarta to protect their underwater settlement. The relationship involves exchange, mutual rescue and cultural boundaries; attacks from outside and the prophecy make coastal defence a real pressure. Asarta is therefore not merely a jealous warmonger: it continually shifts between building ports, maintaining allies and pursuing supernatural power.【Local flavour text】

Its sea route especially stresses the transition from river experience to genuine ocean action. Riverboats cannot handle open-water storms; ports, a usable fleet and merfolk assistance make longer routes possible. For the player, diplomacy, coastal development and naval preparation cannot be replaced entirely by land warfare. Maritime allies are not unconditional tools either: rescue creates requests for protection, while fulfilling promises and earning prophetic prestige are separate tests.【Local script】【Local flavour text】

Its darker side must not be reduced to ordinary sibling rivalry. Later missions require the player to deal with Rayaz loyalists in its former lands. The current English text explicitly demands the destruction of those who still support Sykar's family and compares people who refuse to acknowledge Katyradz to killable “savage” outsiders; another mission uses dehumanising hatred toward humans. The script implements the first policy through a centralisation prerequisite and nationalist rebels in Rayaz's core provinces, rather than leaving it as ignorable narration. The exact casualties in a given campaign require playtesting, but the policy intent is already sufficient to lower the value score sharply.【Local script】【Local flavour text】

The current Mod contains a decision forming S81 Khatalashya, and Asarta is one of its eligible predecessors. Formation enters shared imperial content, while events can still distinguish the origin through was_tag = L96. The core of this article is Asarta's own twenty missions and its sibling-defiance story; shared imperial content with Rayaz or other lizardfolk countries is not counted again as L96-exclusive material.【Local script】

Personality and recommendation

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansion 85/100 | Autocracy 72/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 78/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; thematic intensity 76/100) | Pluralism 25/100. Phase trajectory: the sea-trade and merfolk mutual-aid phase (Pluralism 58) → the loyalist-purge phase (Pluralism 25).

v2.1 values: Evil (22/100), with a declining trajectory. The sea-trade and cultural-revival phase is neutral (58/100), while the policy of eliminating Sykar's loyalists is evil (22/100). Sea trade, Irikin revival and mutual aid with merfolk provide public benefits, but later missions explicitly advocate killing Sykar's loyalists and use dehumanising language about humans; the script contains the associated centralisation and rebel nodes. War and monarchy themselves are not the reasons for deductions. The Chinese source repeats its phase comparison here: sea trade and cultural revival (Neutral, 58/100) → eliminating Sykar's loyalists (Evil, 22/100). Its accompanying explanation credits the genuine public benefits of early cultural revival, sea trade and aid to merfolk, but judges that the later extermination policy and denial of human personhood outweigh them. The deductions do not come from rivalry, conquest or tribal monarchy, but from the concrete killing policy and exclusionary language. This suits players interested in an “unchosen heir” becoming a dark empire, maritime lizardfolk and mutation events. It does not suit players expecting a morally moderate heroic route about defying fate.

Asarta suits players who want an “unchosen heir” defiance story, a maritime lizardfolk route and supernatural events. It is not suited to players expecting a morally gentle underdog story. The official Final Empire release announcement explicitly frames the split between Katyradz and Sykar as part of the update's central storyline. Two player discussions focus on Asarta's opening strategy and the surrounding sibling alliances; neither proves the current mission rewards or random events. See the evidence page for the original research boundary.【Official release context】【Community view】

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here; suspicious percentages or script-valued effects require separate review. Raw script values are shown where appropriate.

Asarta (L96) — Asarta Ideas

Set ID: L96_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = L96 #Asarta
    }

Asarta Traditions

  • Provincial trade power modifier: +10% (global_prov_trade_power_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Military technology cost: -10% (mil_tech_cost_modifier; raw value -0.1).

1. The Middle Son

Katyradz had always lived in the shadow of his elder brother Sykar. He had to watch as Sykar was chosen for greatness by the nagas, destined to overthrow the remnants of Zerat and bring forth the fabled 333rd Empire to unite all lizardfolk. Yet Katyradz held ambitions of his own. Late into the night he pored over historical records of Karassk’s defeat in their wars with Kheterata. Armed with this knowledge and determined to prove his worth, Katyradz took the soldiers of Asarta and launched an invasion of the significantly larger military power of Karassk. If he was to emerge victorious here, surely the nagas would reward his endeavours.

  • Monarch military skill: +1 (monarch_military_power; raw value 1).

2. The Siege of Ashuzal

Sykar of Rayaz knew his younger brother harboured ambitions above what the naga had deemed him worthy of, and held some sympathy for his position. Yet when Katyradz declared war on Karassk, Sykar thought his ambitions had outstripped his capabilities and had no intention of assisting. That was until word reached him that his foolhardy brother had somehow taken the fortress of Ashuzal. How he managed to capture the fortress before reinforcements arrived was beyond Sykar’s understanding. Between the successful siege and news of the Karshyras rebellion, perhaps his brother would succeed in crushing Karassk after all.

  • Siege ability: +10% (siege_ability; raw value 0.10).

3. Brothers in Conflict

"Do you believe that because you have felled the remnants of Anzara that you deserve to rule all lizardkind? That because the naga chose you to sit upon the throne, you have earned this title? To think you parade around these accomplishments as though they prove your worth. Capturing Zerat is akin to stealing fruit from a dying sloth. I will stand for this no longer! From this day forth, I am your enemy. I will prove myself to the naga, to the Riverclaw people, to all lizardfolk, and indeed to you, that I should be the one to lead the 333rd Empire."

  • Katyradz Riverclaw, 1454 AA

  • Change rival cost: -50% (rival_change_cost; raw value -0.5).

  • Power projection from insults: +1 (power_projection_from_insults; raw value 1).

4. Driven from the Gamyi

Across lizardfolk lands stand the zatsarya, towering spires so tall they pierce the clouds themselves. These pillars to the stars were placed by the divine beings to guide the lizardfolk. Many lie in ruin, their tips reaching the treetops, and some no longer reside within lizardfolk territory. Instead they are defiled by human hands, who know nothing of their origin or their importance. We must reclaim what is rightfully ours from their fleshy fingers.

  • Unjustified demands: -20% (unjustified_demands; raw value -0.2).

5. River Transports

The Riverclaw tribes have long been some of the most prosperous people of the lizardfolk, despite its precarious position next to the humans. The many great rivers that flow through the jungles have been an aquatic highway between towns and villages, enabling the swift transportation of goods and people. Before any hatchling can call itself a fully grown lizard, they must be able to construct their own Asarta canoe and captain it to the next village downstream. Although built for river sailing, so sturdy and effective are these vessels that they can, with some adjustments, even brave the open seas.

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

  • Light ship cost: -10% (light_ship_cost; raw value -0.1).

6. Isagumze’s Invasion

Decades of fighting amongst lizardfolk nations vying for the title of the 333rd Empire, meant that the forces of Asarta were ill-prepared for when the humans attacked. At first the forces of Isagumze and Kuiika swept across the rivers and through the jungles, burning down villages in their wake, armed with new gunpowder weapons they had secured from foreign traders.

However, Asarta was able to outlast them. They refused to face them head-on, retreating steadily as the humans pushed deeper into lizardfolk territory. Eventually the humans were bogged down and exhausted, forced to abandon their weapons as they became inoperable due to tropical monsoons. It was then that the forces of Asarta struck, forcing the humans to flee back beyond the rivers from whence they came.

  • Maximum general maneuver: +1 (max_general_maneuver; raw value 1).

  • War exhaustion cost: -25% (war_exhaustion_cost; raw value -0.25).

7. Felling Dragons

Despite their scaled hides, dragons share little in common with the lizardfolk. None have terrorized the lizardfolk in an age, although word had spread of one with bronze scales who had made a home in Aramoole. With the threat of dragonfire so close by, the Arraskay lizardfolk created a mortar cannon designed to take such a beast out of the sky. Called the Draktaya, or Dragonslayer, its shells explode mid-flight in a shower of magically-enhanced chemicals that can seemingly melt through anything, be it flesh, scales, or indeed bronze. Should the bronze dragon dare to soar above our soldiers, our artillery shall be there to strike it out of the sky.

  • Back-Row Artillery Damage: +10% (backrow_artillery_damage; raw value 0.10).

Asarta Ambitions

  • Free diplomatic policies: +1 (free_dip_policy; raw value 1).

Three River Traditions

  • Hostile Attrition: +100% (hostile_attrition; raw value 1).

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).

1. Three River Tribes

Asarta, Arazin and Rayaz tribes are three ancient tribes, that inhabited the area between Zerat and Karassk for centuries. While for most of their history they were dependent on one of the great cities, and sometimes their overlords were different, tribes never forgot their bonds, which tied them close throughout centuries (placeholder)

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

2. Between Great Cities

All three tribes are located between Karassk and Zerat, which allows them control the trade between two wealthiest lizardfolk cities. (placeholder)

  • Caravan power: +20% (caravan_power; raw value 0.2).

3. Zianysha Warfare

Zianysha - are thin river boats lizardfolk learned to craft since time immemorial. However, river tribes learned to use them for quick movement and raids on their enemies, which allowed them to be a fearsome force near rivers. (placeholder)

  • Movement speed: +10% (movement_speed; raw value 0.10).

  • Infantry combat ability: +5% (infantry_power; raw value 0.05).

4. Destined Conquerors

An old tale prophesies that once all three river tribes will be granted leaders, which will unite both Karassk and Zerat under their rule. (placeholder)

  • Land force limit modifier: +10% (land_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.10).

  • global_manpower_modifier: +10% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.10).

5. Boat Markets

Wondering bazaars on boats (placeholder)

  • Number of merchants: +1 (merchants; raw value 1).

6. Naga Storytellers

Nagas educate youth of river tribes since time immemorial, and that earns them loyalty of river tribes (placeholder)

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

7. Metalworking Traditions

Huge deposits of metals supported long tradition of metalworking (placeholder)

  • Shock damage: +5% (shock_damage; raw value 0.05).

  • Production efficiency: +5% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.05).
